subtitle: A private daily journal
promotionalText: One gentle prompt a day. Write, speak, or draw your answer. Passcode and Face ID, everything stays on your phone. No account, no cloud, no ads.
description:
Permission is a quiet, private place to come home to yourself — one gentle prompt a day, kept just for you.

Open the app and today's invitation is waiting: a single, kind question to sit with. There is no streak to protect, no feed to scroll, no one watching. Answer it the way that feels right today, or simply read it and let it settle.

THREE WAYS TO ANSWER
• Write — type as much or as little as you like
• Speak — record your voice and let the app transcribe it for you
• Draw — sketch your answer with your finger

YOUR PAGES, KEPT PRIVATELY
• A notebook holds everything you've written, spoken and drawn, in one calm place
• Export a copy as a page or a PDF whenever you want one — nothing leaves your phone unless you choose to share it

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
• Lock the app with a 4-digit passcode, and unlock with Face ID or Touch ID
• Everything you write, say or draw stays on this phone
• No account, no sign-in, no cloud, no ads, no tracking, no analytics — the app makes no network connections at all

Permission grew out of Jessica Leigh Biles' "Permission to Begin" work on reconnecting with yourself — gently giving yourself permission to show up, one honest moment at a time. It's free, and it's yours.

A companion to Slow Burn, the private closeness program from the same creators.
